newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on light liquidity, soft peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on light liquidity, soft peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 25 basis points in early trade to 18.25 percent on what dealers said was demand for cash ahead of the weekend.
"Rates usually go up on Fridays on demand for cash, and from players who jack rates up to get a better return over the weekend," a dealer said.
Dealers said a weaker peso and higher U.S. long bond yields provided more upside pressure on Mexican secondary rates.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 0.3 centavo softer at 7.7670/7.7680 per dollar, while the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 11/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile opened up 10 basis points at 18.60 pesos.
Liquidity of 1.275 billion pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations. Dealers also expected an estimated one billion pesos in cash to flow into the market.
